newsitem.title: USA: Detroit mayor sets sights on even higher ratings.
newsitem.headline: Detroit mayor sets sights on even higher ratings.

text.p: Riding a wave of municipal bond rating improvements over the past week, Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer said on Friday he would now work harder to justify those improvements and put the city in a position to achieve even higher credit ratings.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, Archer said he wants to "nudge" his city's ratings toward the top ratings.
Last week, Moody's Investors service restored the Motor City's investment grade rating by upgrading the rating for Detroit's unlimited tax general obligation debt to Baa from Ba1.

On Tuesday, Standard & Poor's Corp. revised its rating outlook to positive from stable and on Thursday Fitch Investors Service upgraded to BBB from BBB-minus its rating on the city's unlimited and limited tax GO debt.
The rating actions were taken as the city prepared an approximately $54 million new and refunded unlimited tax GO bond issue for sale through a syndicate led by J.P. Morgan Securities Inc.
Archer called the positive rating actions "an independent appraisal for the contributions that everybody has tried to make to better the city."

He acknowledged that Detroit still has a way to go and that certain risks, outlined by the rating agencies, still remain in the future, including the city's reliance on automotive-related manufacturing.

Archer said the city, with the help of the corporate community, was striving to diversify its economic base with such projects as planned professional sports stadiums in downtown Detroit for the Tigers baseball team and Lions football team.
A vote in Wayne County on lodging and car rental taxes to help back bonds for the Lions stadium project is scheduled for November 5.

Voters across Michigan will also decide that day whether to allow up to three casinos in Detroit. If approved, the city would receive 55 percent of a state tax on gross gaming revenues, with the rest going to Michigan's school aid fund.
Archer said the casinos would produce 11,000 direct jobs.
Another major development cited by the rating agencies was General Motors Corp.'s announcement earlier this year that it would move its headquarters to the Renaissance Center in downtown Detroit.
